newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares pulled higher by OMV.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares pulled higher by OMV.

text.p: Austrian shares closed at a new high on Tuesday, buoyed by continued demand for energy and chemicals group OMV, and traders said the ATX index could climb to 1,300 points this week.
The blue-chip ATX firmed 19.05 points, or 1.52 percent, to end at 1,270.36, surpassing the previous high set on May 14. Earlier the index touched an intra-day high of 1,276.02.
"OMV is pulling the whole market higher. It's a puzzle where all the money is coming from," a trader said.
OMV was by far the biggest gainer, surging 6.83 percent to 1,535 schillings on a brisk 117,949 contracts.
One market participant traced OMV's strength to persistent rumours that the stock had been incorporated in an international performance index.
Overall 13 ATX shares ended up and eight down.
Industrial group Radex-Heraklith, regional utility EVN, steel firm VA Stahl and Creditanstalt banking shares were all well sought, traders said.
"If the buying interest is sustained, the 1,300 points mark is a realistic target for this week," a trader said.
Insurer Wiener Staedtische was the day's leading decliner, down 1.74 pct at 1,016 schillings.
In continuous trade outside the ATX, do-it-yourself firm bauMax fell eight schillings to 340 after the firm said it was cutting its 1996 dividend and issuing bonus shares.
June ATX futures were 19 points higher at 1,269.0. The broad-based Vienna bourse index firmed 4.81 points, or 1.03 percent, to 469.78. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 254
